newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spanish government bonds made fresh gains on Thursday, and the long bond future closed at 117.80, above resistance at 117.70, suggesting a bullish outlook also for Friday's session, dealers said.

"During the afternoon our market suddenly jumped higher, together with Bunds. Bonos climbed 15 basis points with a single order...I guess it was an order from a hedge fund," said Jose Ramon Arechederra, a trader at ABN Amro in Madrid.
"Bonos broke the tight narrow range they were trapped in. Tomorrow they can gain even more than that and head toward a record high of 118.12," a dealer in Natwest said.
"After tomorrow's possible gains, the market next week is likely to focus on the French audit's results and then on (Federal Reserve Chairman Alan) Greenspan's speech," a dealer said.
Results of the French audit will be made public in Paris on July 21.
The Spanish 10-year spread over Bunds ended at 63 basis points virtually unchanged from this morning.
The peseta fell a bit versus the mark after dealer talk of intervention when the mark hit a record low at 84.13.
